_readme: Page-to-content index for Milad-e-Akbar.pdf, built by visually reading all 87 scanned pages.
`page` / `endPage` are PDF/scan sequence numbers (1-87), matching pdftoppm order — NOT the book's own printed folio numbers (front matter is unnumbered, so the two drift apart).
PDF pages 4 and 5 are byte-identical duplicate scans of the same physical page, as are pages 35 and 36. No content is missing — just don't render the duplicate twice.

The book does not label sections as Hamd/Naat/Salam/Manqabat. It uses generic form-labels (Ghazal, Qasida, Qit'a, Abyat, Musaddas, Ash'ar, Deegar/'more') and the devotional category has to be inferred from content (who is being addressed). `bookLabel` = the literal label printed in the book (null if the poem is unlabeled). `suggestedSection` = inferred category, using an EXTENDED set beyond your current MiladEntry union — see _schemaNote.
`title` is a transliteration of the opening line/refrain, not an official title (this book mostly doesn't name its poems).
Prose narrative / discourse sections are included too (suggestedSection: 'Narrative') since they're structurally important for a reader/reciter app, even though they're not verse.
Verses are NOT transcribed here — this is a structural index only. Transcribing all verses into Urdu+Roman per the Verse type would be a much larger follow-on pass.
_schemaNote: Recommend extending MiladEntry['section'] from "Hamd" | "Naat" | "Salam" | "Manqabat" to also include "Durood" | "Munajat" | "Lori" | "Tazmeen" | "Miracle" | "Narrative" (front matter, hikayat/miracle prose, and Mi'raj narrative genuinely don't fit the original four).
